title: Salt That Never Stops Forming
logline: In shallow coastal pans, salt crystals form, are raked away, and form again within days, a heap that always looks the same because it is never actually the same crystal twice.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Along the southern coast from the cinnamon belt to the dry-zone salt pans: from senses working together to a heap that looks unchanged though no crystal in it is the same twice.

thread_out.thread: The salt pans' daylight turns to a lagoon at night, where most of what reaches the crew, a flicker, a splash, never becomes a decision.

requirements: An active coastal salt-pan operation willing to allow filming across a working cycle
Time on location across several days or weeks to observe a full cycle
Consent that includes the workers' economic situation, not only the visual cycle

suggestions.why: A well-known traditional salt-production area on the southern dry-zone coast.
suggestions.season_notes: Salt production is tied to the dry season; timing would need to match an active harvest cycle.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A heap of salt can look the same all season while every grain in it is new. The Abhidhamma describes solid things the same way: countless tiny parts that each last a moment and are constantly replaced, so the whole seems not to change.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: සීසනය පුරා එකම ලෙස පෙනෙන ලුණු ගොඩේ කැට නිතරම අලුත් වනවා සේම, ඝන දේවල්ද ඒවායේ කුඩා කොටස් නොනවත්වා බිඳී අලුත් වන නිසා නොවෙනස්ව පෙනෙන බව අභිධර්මය කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts teach that material phenomena have a lifespan of seventeen mind-moments, with an arising, a long standing phase and a dissolving (C039). Margaya explains why objects still seem to last for months and years: like a sand heap seen from a distance, every object is a cluster of countless tiny units (rūpa-kalāpa) that do not all break at once, and each unit that breaks is replaced by a new one in the same place (C039). The texts also teach that for beings with a body, mind rests on this living matter, since each sense-consciousness arises on a physical base (C037).
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Across a season the camera keeps returning to the same pans: brine let in, crystals forming at the edges over days, raking, carrying, a heap softened by rain and built again. The heap in the last shot looks like the heap in the first, and the workers' own account of the cycle lets the viewer realise that it is made of entirely different salt.

key_terms.en: cluster of material phenomena; the smallest unit things are built from

lesson.caution: The seventeen moments are not a measurable time and the clusters are not atoms or cells; the texts draw no 'everything changes, so let go' moral from this.
lesson.builds_on: Where the cinnamon shed showed a judgement assembled from separate senses, this film turns to the things those senses meet and finds that what looks solid and still is being renewed all the time.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
